svg.title: Merge: fixed arrays and moving indices
svg.desc: Merge the two sorted ranges of one array, 3, 7 and 2, 5. low is 0, mid is 1, high is 3. All four input cells stay visible. Consumed input values are faded, never removed. The four-slot temporary vector begins with four zeros. Indices i and j mark the next unread input, and k marks the next temporary slot to write. Copy 2, 3, 5, then 7 into the existing temp slots. When j is 4 the right half is exhausted; when i is 2 the left half is exhausted. When k is 4 the temporary array is full. Finally copy all four temporary values back into arr, producing 2, 3, 5, 7. Neither array changes size. A visual gap separates the two input halves during merging. In the final copy-back step, arr is drawn as one contiguous sorted array. Index markers appear above the cells.
svg.text: low = 0, mid = 1, high = 3. Both arrays have 4 slots throughout.
Faded input = already copied; green temp = merged output.
temp = [0, 0, 0, 0]. No merged values have been written.
Step 1: Copy 2 from the right half
Step 2: Copy 3 from the left half
Step 3: Copy 5 from the right half
j = 4 > high: right half exhausted; i = 1 <= mid.
Step 5: Copy temp back to arr
The input range is now sorted: [2, 3, 5, 7].
